newsitem.title: ITALY: Dini says Italy budget deal needs more study.
newsitem.headline: Dini says Italy budget deal needs more study.

text.p: Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, leader of the centrist Italian Renewal party, said on Wednesday that a deal among government coalition parties on a corrective supplementary budget needed further study.
Dini told reporters that a meeting of party leaders on the contents of the budget package, expected to be approved at a cabinet meeting on Thursday, had been worthwhile.
"This morning's meeting was useful," Dini said. "There are still important issues to be studied (and) it will be up to the cabinet to decide tomorrow morning," he said.

The mini-budget is expected to include up to around 16 trillion lire ($9.5 billion) of deficit-cutting measures to try to keep the 1997 deficit on track to meet the limits required for founder membership of economic and monetary union (EMU).

Dini's party had been pushing for the government to embark on an overhaul of the welfare state with the mini-budget and has been critical of provisions to raise cash by getting firms to pay taxes on their severance payment funds ahead of schedule.

Fausto Bertinotti, head of the hardleft Communist Refoundation party that ensures the government's survival in parliament, said earlier that he had won his battle to prevent any further tax hikes or cuts to social spending.
"The (corrective) budget contains measures indicated by the government and not by Bertinotti," Dini said.
